**Yes, exactly.** 

When you press `Alt + Space`, it is 100% interacting with your custom build rather than the official one. Here is why:

1. **The Active Server Daemon**: Vicinae operates on a client-server architecture. The process listening for shortcut triggers and rendering the UI window is the background daemon (`vicinae-server`). We verified that the running daemon (managed by systemd) is `/usr/local/libexec/vicinae/vicinae-server`, running your custom commit `c038ef43a`.
2. **PATH & CLI Precedence**: If your window manager or desktop shortcut executes the CLI command `vicinae toggle` on `Alt + Space`, `/usr/local/bin/vicinae` has higher priority in your system's `PATH` than `/usr/bin/vicinae`, ensuring the custom binary always handles the invocation.

Every time you bring up the launcher with `Alt + Space`, you are using your custom build with all the ported Raycast features (acronym search, instant math intent, plain-text paste, snap layouts, etc.).
